title: Prepare for product manager interviews
summary: Interviews usually test how you think about users, how you make and measure decisions and how you work with others. Practise out loud with real examples.

beginner: Learn the usual kinds of question: motivation ('why product, why us'), product sense (how you would approach a user problem), execution and metrics (how you would measure or respond to a change), prioritisation and behavioural stories.

Prepare six stories from your work and your practice project: a decision made with little data, a disagreement, a failure, a time you influenced without authority, a time you used data and a time you learned from users. Write each as situation, action and result.

For product sense questions, use a simple structure: clarify the goal, identify users and their pain points, generate options, choose one with reasons, say how you would measure success and name the risks.
Practise metrics questions with your notes on numbers: define the metric, name a guardrail and explain how you would check a drop.
Research the company. Use the product, read its public material and prepare three questions about how the team decides and measures.
Practise out loud with a friend, a PM from your conversations or an AI tool, and ask for one thing to improve each time.
After each interview, write what went well, what you would change and what you learned, and send a short thank-you.

toolExamples.claude: Ask it to act as an interviewer, ask follow-up questions and tell you one thing to improve. Do not paste in anything confidential.
toolExamples.notion: Keep your stories on cards: situation, action, result and what you learned.

definitionOfDone: One product sense answer and one metrics answer practised out loud
Three questions prepared for each company
A short review written after each interview
pitfalls: Reciting frameworks without thinking about the user
Stories with no result and no numbers

sources.title: A guide to breaking into product management (Mind the Product)
